Plus, you’ll be supporting independent journalism—which, can you even imagine not supporting independent journalism in times like these? Yikes. Click here to subscribe.
results.summary:
A new investigation by Gamers Nexus reveals that certain LG smart TVs continue to collect user data and record ambient audio even when the devices are powered off.

### Key Points
- Researchers found that LG smart TVs use Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) to scan local Wi-Fi networks and identify connected devices like smartphones and watches.
- The investigation claims the TVs store audio data locally when disconnected from the internet, transmitting the information once a connection is restored.
- Security experts identified vulnerabilities in the TV software that could potentially allow hackers to exploit these data-gathering features.
- LG has not issued a formal response to the findings, which contradict the company's previous claims that it does not record ambient conversations.
- The report highlights that these data collection practices often remain active unless users manually navigate complex settings menus to disable them.

### Why it Matters
This investigation highlights the growing tension between consumer privacy and the aggressive data-harvesting practices embedded in modern internet-connected home appliances. The findings may trigger regulatory scrutiny similar to recent legal actions taken against other manufacturers regarding unauthorized data collection and advertising practices.

results.title: People’s Picks: 4 Phone Brands Dominate, but 1 Reigns Supreme and It’s Not Apple
results.author: Dashia Milden
results.content:
Every few years, you may think about upgrading your smartphone. A lot of thought and research goes into your next choice, whether it’s the price, features or brand reputation. Maybe you’re eyeing the latest and greatest, or considering a different phone brand or model altogether. Our readers’ opinions may help you decide.
CNET’s People’s Picks dives into what our readers really think about their tech devices and services, like their internet service provider, TVs and even their mobile carrier.
This round was all about readers’ phone brands, just in time for Apple’s Sept. 9 Surprise and shine event, where we expect new iPhone models to be revealed. We asked about everything from brand loyalty to battery life, durability and even price-to-value. The results came down to four big-name tech brands. While there’s only one overall winner, other brands win in key categories that can make a big difference in your day-to-day tasks if you’re upgrading soon.
Overall winner: Google
Google is the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Picks for Phones. CNET averaged the scores across three categories to determine the overall satisfaction rating, which includes customer satisfaction, battery longevity and price-to-value.
Google wins with a score of 4.52 out of 5, while Motorola trails closely behind with 4.45.
“It’s no surprise to me that Google and Motorola scored top marks because both sell some of the most affordable phones that people can buy. Motorola’s Moto G series costs hundreds of dollars less than Apple’s cheapest iPhone,” said CNET’s Director of Content, Patrick Holland. “At $500, Google’s Pixel 10A is one of the best values that you can buy today, especially as phone prices spike due to the ongoing RAM shortage caused by AI and data centers. It just goes to show that in 2026, you can spend less than $500 and still have a great phone that lasts you years.”
On the other hand, Samsung and Apple trail behind with scores of 4.19 and 3.87, respectively. Both brands have evolved in the smartphone space with AI-powered features, upgraded cameras, and thinner phone designs, but fell short in this category.
“There are a few factors at play here, most notably that Google and Motorola ship a fraction of the phones that Samsung does — so Pixel and Razr buyers are a more devoted core of customers than the many who buy Galaxy phones,” said CNET Managing Editor of Mobile David Lumb. A Counterpoint Research report on phone shipments in the first quarter of 2026 noted that Google (3% of the US market) and Motorola (10%) combined accounted for half of Samsung’s market share (26%).
The other thing to remember is that Google sells mostly premium phones.
“Aside from the Pixel 10A as a midrange device. Motorola and Samsung have wider ranges of more affordable and cheap phones, so I’d guess there’s less consumer fondness at the lower end of the device price scale,” Lumb said.
Apple’s fourth-place spot is a tougher nut to crack. Perhaps consumers haven’t seen as many upgrades in successive years as they would like in new iPhones, or they’re miffed at the higher prices Apple’s phones sell for. What’s most likely the case, Lumb suggested, is that there are simply more people buying new iPhones. In the Counterpoint report above, Apple handsets accounted for 58% of all phones shipped in the US.
AI features
AI features like photo editing, live translation and AI-powered summaries are becoming the focal point for new smartphone models. But what matters more is how much you’ll use those built-in features. Google Pixel wins with 88% of its users saying their phone’s AI features are essential and occasionally useful.
“Out of the four brands, only one is a true AI company, and that’s Google. In fact, Google’s Gemini AI can run on phones from all four brands, including the iPhone via an app. The Gemini Assistant can be used on Motorola and Samsung phones,” said Holland.
Lumb added that Google has led the charge in both including and promoting AI features in its Pixel phones that people actually use, like Magic Eraser and live translation.
“Pixel owners have been using AI features for years, and combined with Google aggressively inserting its Gemini assistant throughout the phone, it makes sense that Samsung Galaxy owners would feel a lesser impact from AI.”
Samsung has made plenty of AI advancements, like a health assistant and browser upgrades, but it falls behind, with only 64% of its users saying the same. Apple and Motorola trail behind with 14% and 8% each. Most Motorola users say the phone lacked built-in tools or ignored them.
What few AI features are available on iPhones were introduced more recently, so it’s unsurprising that their owners wouldn’t consider them essential to daily use, Lumb said. While Gemini continues to evolve, Apple’s advanced AI Siri was delayed for years and will finally launch with the upcoming iOS 27. 
Battery life
Ties with Motorola 
For a phone’s battery to exceed expectations, it must last a day or more. Motorola and Google tie in this category, with 74% saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations by lasting a full day or longer without needing to be charged. Comparatively, Samsung and Apple fall behind, with only about half (52%) saying their phones’ batteries exceed expectations, while others say they just meet expectations. Apple finishes last, with only 31% reporting the same for their iPhones’ batteries. Most said their phone needed to be charged midday. 
“The number one factor for battery life is how you use your phone. And I think this result speaks volumes about how much iPhone owners are on their phones,” said Holland.
CNET’s phone battery testing found that Apple’s phones had the longest battery life, with OnePlus placing second and Motorola third. However, the test doesn’t account for how you use your phone specifically each day – everyone is different. If you’re hyper-connected and your default is scrolling through social media apps or streaming videos, even the best battery life won’t be enough for you, Holland said. “Thankfully, Google, Motorola and Samsung, along with Apple, have all increased the charging speeds on their handsets to at least make topping them off less of a pain point.”
Motorola
Value
Motorola wins in price-to-value, with 82% of its readers saying it offers exceptional value by delivering more than its price suggests. Only 4% rate the brand as overpriced.
“Before Motorola brought back the Razr as a foldable phone, its most popular handsets were its Moto G line that start as low as $200 and top out at $350,” said Holland. “Motorola has deep, long-term relationships with phone carriers, which often sell these phones at a discount.”
Compared with other brands, 45% of Pixel owners say Google’s phone offers exceptional value, and 35% of Samsung users say the same.
The surprising fact is that Apple places fourth in this category, with 58% of iPhone users saying it’s overpriced. Only 12% find the phone’s value exceptional. However, many tech brands are raising prices due to the RAM shortage, which makes it tough to determine what’s worth the high cost.
“The only company that hasn’t raised prices on its phones this year is Apple. There’s a chance it might announce a price hike at its Sept. 9 event. The cheapest iPhone the company sells starts at $600. You can find incredible Android phones for less, like the Google Pixel 10A for $500,” said Holland.
Apple
Durability
Choosing a phone that doesn’t shatter, crack or leave you with a broken camera can make a big difference when you need one to last a few years. Some phones are more durable than others. Apple wins this category with 78% of readers saying it’s highly durable against drops and daily use with minimal to no damage. The remaining 22% either deal with normal wear and minor scuffs over time, report their phone as fragile or always have a heavy-duty case to protect it.
Holland said that when Apple released the iPhone 12 in 2020, it was the first to have a flat, dense build with squared-off sides to increase durability. In the years following, Samsung followed suit, adopting a flat build for its Galaxy S and S Plus models, and Google implemented a similar design with its Pixel phones.
Google follows closely behind with 72% saying their Pixel smartphone is highly durable, while 28% say it’s moderately durable.
Not as many readers with a Motorola say the phone is highly durable (65%), but even fewer readers with a Samsung (58%) phone say the same. Samsung users say their foldable phone and screens are fragile and only moderately durable. Some readers criticize the brand for the phone’s fragility and susceptibility to damage from drops.
Brand retention and loyalty
Despite Apple falling short in several categories, 86% of Apple users said they’re extremely likely to buy the same brand next time.
“Apple’s most popular product is the iPhone, but its iPhone-only features like iMessage and FaceTime, not found on Android, that keep people tied in,” said Holland. “Also, if you want to learn about how to use your iPhone or get it fixed, you can go to the Apple Store and talk with an actual human – I think those retail stores are Apple’s secret weapon.”
Whereas 79% of Samsung owners share the same sentiment for the brand. Over half of Google Pixel owners (58%) would buy a Google phone again, but only 42% of people with Motorola phones would. Other Motorola owners are using competitor research to determine their next phone purchase.
Methodology
CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,107 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from July 1 to July 28, 2026.
results.summary:
Google has been named the overall winner in CNET’s 2026 People’s Picks for smartphones, outperforming Motorola, Samsung, and Apple in key categories like customer satisfaction and battery longevity.

### Key Points
- Google secured the top spot with a 4.52 out of 5 satisfaction rating, followed by Motorola at 4.45.
- Motorola ranked highest for price-to-value, with 82% of users reporting exceptional value for their devices.
- Apple led the durability category, with 78% of users praising the iPhone's resistance to drops and daily wear.
- Google Pixel users reported the highest engagement with AI features, with 88% finding them essential or useful.
- Apple maintains the highest brand loyalty, as 86% of iPhone owners stated they are extremely likely to purchase the brand again.
- The survey, conducted by Alchemer, gathered data from 1,107 U.S. adults between July 1 and July 28, 2026.

### Why it Matters
These results highlight a growing consumer preference for affordable, high-value devices over premium-priced handsets in a market impacted by rising hardware costs. While Apple retains strong brand loyalty through its ecosystem, the data suggests that competitors are successfully capturing market share by delivering superior battery performance and practical AI integration.

results.title: Mathspace breach exposes data on over a million students and parents
results.author: Sinisa Markovic
results.content:
Mathspace breach exposes data on over a million students and parents
Mathspace has confirmed that attackers broke into its internal reporting system through an unpatched Metabase vulnerability and stole data belonging to more than a million students, parents, and school staff.
The Sydney-based maths education company wrote in a blog post that the vulnerability, in its self-hosted installation of Metabase, allowed attackers to obtain administrator access to the system without a legitimate login.
Metabase is a business intelligence tool used to connect to and explore company databases. It’s available as a free open-source, self-hosted version, or as a paid service with cloud and self-hosted options.
“On 3 September 2026, we confirmed that unauthorised parties had accessed an internal reporting system used by Mathspace and downloaded information on students, their parents or guardians, and school staff,” said Alvin Savoy CTO at Mathspace.
“Our investigation identified unauthorised access dating back to 10 August 2026, Australian Eastern Standard Time. We confirmed that information was downloaded from our Australian reporting database on 27 August,” added Savoy.
According to the company, the breach affected 1,079,819 people in total, all located in Australia and New Zealand.
The exposed data included usernames, first and last names, email addresses, country, time zone, user type, email-verification status, last-active date, last-login date, and date joined. Some of these are internal Mathspace identifiers tied to student accounts.
Mathspace said no academic records, assessment results, passwords, authentication tokens, or API credentials were exposed. The exposed data did not include records linking user accounts to their schools, though it said this may still be possible for schools with identifiable email domains.
“Customer passwords, single sign-on (SSO) tokens and other customer authentication credentials were not exposed,” Savoy noted.
“We have no evidence so far that the data has been published, distributed, sold or otherwise misused.”
Mathspace isn’t requiring a password reset, since login credentials weren’t exposed. It is warning, however, that the leaked names and email addresses could be used to make phishing attempts look convincing.
Savoy is advising users to be wary of unexpected messages, never share passwords or verification codes, and use a unique password for every account.
“Based on our investigation to date, you can continue using Mathspace for lessons and assignments. The affected internal reporting system has been taken offline,” Savoy concluded.
This is not an isolated case in which attackers used a vulnerability in Metabase to reach customer data. Framework, Tally, and Kilo Code all disclosed similar breaches in August 2026, after attackers exploited the same SQL injection flaw in their Metabase instances.
results.summary:
Mathspace has confirmed a data breach affecting over one million users in Australia and New Zealand after attackers exploited an unpatched vulnerability in its internal reporting software.

### Key Points
- Attackers accessed the Mathspace reporting system between August 10 and August 27, 2026, by exploiting a known vulnerability in a self-hosted Metabase instance.
- The breach exposed the personal information of 1,079,819 students, parents, and school staff, including names, email addresses, and account activity timestamps.
- Mathspace stated that no passwords, academic records, or authentication tokens were compromised during the unauthorized access.
- The company has taken the affected reporting system offline and confirmed that no evidence currently suggests the stolen data has been sold or misused.
- Similar Metabase-related security incidents were reported by companies including Framework, Tally, and Kilo Code throughout August 2026.

### Why it Matters
This incident highlights the significant security risks associated with unpatched third-party business intelligence tools integrated into educational platforms. While sensitive academic records remain secure, the exposure of contact information increases the risk of targeted phishing attacks against students and their families.

results.title: DLSS 5 proves that Nvidia has lost the plot
results.author: Dipan Saha
results.content:
DLSS 5 received an immensely negative reaction from players when it was first revealed in early 2026, and it seems Nvidia has not taken those complaints to heart. Instead, it doubled down, and the latest work-in-progress leaked build is a mixed bag.
While DLSS 5 looks genuinely good in certain select scenarios, it’s not what this is about. Nvidia’s slop filter introduces unnecessary detail and “realism”, which drastically alters the game beyond its intended look, and could set a dangerous precedent.
DLSS 5 destroys the original artistic vision of the game
Chasing realism isn’t what games are always about
DLSS 5 is not an upscaler. In fact, it actively alters the output and enhances it further, using generative AI to “render” a more photorealistic image. This makes it more computationally expensive compared to traditional DLSS, which kind of defeats the whole point of the tech, but I’m getting ahead of myself here…
And the results have been quite varied, to say the least. DLSS 5 seems to work best under older titles, bringing them to a modern “RTX remaster” equivalent. That is, until you look into the finer details.
DLSS 5 is way too strong of a filter, and much of the remastering done here is full of flaws, as you’d expect from any kind of AI-generated frame. Not to mention it looks downright terrible on many titles, with Final Fantasy VII Remake’s Cloud being the stuff of nightmares.
If anything, though, DLSS 5 ruins a game's graphical presentation. Games are designed with certain visual elements in mind, and forcibly applying a filter to change things so dramatically just doesn’t sit right with me.
Sure, you could argue that mods and reshade packs do the same thing, but Nvidia’s new shiny upscaler looks a lot worse in comparison. Not to mention, these community-driven shaders were created with intent — with each section of a game hand-crafted to suit the author’s tastes.
DLSS 5 in its current (beta) state is just a photorealism filter, and not all games aim for that. While Nvidia has confirmed that developers can fine-tune the DLSS 5 output to maintain the “original” artistic vision, it begs the question: why even ship games that need a visual filter to look as intended?
DLSS 5 has a massive impact on performance
And requires specific hardware to work
It’s not like DLSS 5 is a lightweight model either. Oh no, far from it — and the “upscaler” has been seen to slash frame rates by up to 50%, mandating the use of both traditional DLSS upscaling and frame generation to offset the difference, which works as well as you’d expect.
To make matters worse, it is also currently restricted to the RTX 5000 (Blackwell) Series, which means you’ll need a rather pricey GPU to even stand a chance at previewing this tech. You won’t be able to use this on something like an RTX 5060 well at all.
Nvidia plans to port it to the RTX 4000 Series later, although I wouldn’t be too optimistic about performance. Restricting the tech to current-gen cards that are mostly out of reach for most folks isn't a great outlook.
The so-called improvements on offer simply aren't worth the performance loss, and a broad majority will largely ignore them.
As the technology matures, it could slowly turn into a crutch
Another ray tracing-like situation could be on the horizon
I fear the worst with the eventual, full release of DLSS 5. The current crop of game tech, especially ray tracing and upscaling, has been a bane for gaming in recent years. While these were made with good intent, most games still overutilize them, to the point that they've become more of a crutch.
Running a modern AAA game at higher resolutions without upscaling often tanks frame rates below 60 FPS, making it mandatory no matter the card you use. The same can be said for ray tracing, which is being forced on every game these days.
DLSS 5 could pose a different kind of problem, though. By actively altering the game’s look, it could push developers to optimize for a DLSS 5 “exclusive” look, and because it would be gated behind specific GPUs, it would ultimately severely restrict the number of players who could achieve that “final” level of detail.
DLSS 5 is trying to solve a problem that does not exist
To address the elephant in the room, DLSS 5 is trying to solve a problem that doesn't exist. Just play games the way they were meant to look in the first place. This kind of implementation has absolutely zero reason to exist and is a slap in the face to most designers.
If anything, it could set off a wave of DLSS 5 “enhanced” titles that force the tech to be used. It really makes you think, though: Why not just design the game with the original look and intent (without relying on an AI filter to enhance things over), instead of producing generic, photorealistic abominations?
Until then, there’s not much to do but hope that AMD doesn’t follow suit, along with the rest of the industry.
results.summary:
Nvidia’s upcoming DLSS 5 technology faces significant criticism for using generative AI to alter game aesthetics, causing performance drops of up to 50% on high-end Blackwell GPUs.

### Key Points
- DLSS 5 functions as a photorealism filter rather than a traditional upscaler, often overriding the original artistic intent of game developers.
- Early testing shows inconsistent visual quality, with reports of distorted character models and graphical artifacts in titles like Final Fantasy VII Remake.
- The technology is currently restricted to Nvidia’s RTX 5000-series graphics cards, with future support planned for the RTX 4000-series.
- Enabling the feature can reduce frame rates by as much as 50%, necessitating the simultaneous use of traditional upscaling and frame generation.
- Critics argue the tech acts as a performance-heavy crutch that may pressure developers to design games specifically for AI-enhanced visual outputs.

### Why it Matters
This technology represents a shift toward AI-driven visual modification that could fundamentally change how games are developed and experienced. If widely adopted, it risks creating a hardware-gated standard that prioritizes synthetic photorealism over the original creative vision of game designers.
